title: CMake: Add -Wmissing-variable-declarations
description:
Clang (C and C++) and gcc (C-only) warning for global variables
defined without a previous declaration. This can be used to find
global variables that really should be static (or instead should
be declared extern in a header file in some cases).
    
It is blocked for now for plugins due to the required versioning
symbols. Perhaps there could be a common plugin header file that
would declare the symbols?

AI-Assisted: no

notes.body: mentioned in merge request !24826

Sounds like a good idea - maybe we could just not set the flag for the plugins folder?  I would say that check_static.py probably flags more functions than variables - is there an equivalent for functions (we already use -Wmissing-declarations) ?

We aren't actually using -Wmissing-declarations for similar reasons.  As stated in the comments, the dissector registration architecture seems to prohibit it being enabled.

But I agree that this is a much better approach that writing our own scripts
Right. The dissector registration functions are trickier because they all have distinct names. The plugin variables are bit easier because they're all the same name, so we could have a common header.

I rearranged the CMakeLists a bit and exempted that directory.

Might need to change the CMakeListsCustom.txt.example a bit, but otherwise this is ready for now.
I added something to remove the "plugins" prefix from a specified plugins source directory, in order to be backwards compatible with existing `CMakeListsCustom.txt` files.

Apparently `__private_extern__` is a deprecated Apple Clang only feature, and supposedly it is the same as hidden visibility for non static symbols.

Though there are people who report using static and inline assembly for this:
https://alastairs-place.net/blog/2013/01/10/interesting-os-x-crash-report-tidbits/
https://gist.github.com/swillits/12c01638dbd7c488fd30

But has anybody gotten it to properly decorate crash reports with application-specific information in recent versions of macOS? It wasn't doing it for me on Tahoe.

(Perhaps they don't want malicious software suppliers to use it as a sneaky way of exfiltrating data from a user's machine, if they've signed up to have Apple feed them crash reports?)

I'm not sure why check_static.py didn't see some of the dissector issues - maybe now it can be retired.  One thing it does flag are functions that are declared in header files but nothing ever calls them, I've been cautious about removing those because someone may have private dissectors that do use them..

I think some of them at least are where a variable was declared (and used) with `extern` in another translation unit source instead of in a header, so the compilers warn but perhaps the script did not?
A few were declared in a header, but the translation unit defining it didn't include its own header, only other translation units did.

> One thing it does flag are functions that are declared in header files but nothing ever calls them, I've been cautious about removing those because someone may have private dissectors that do use them.

If a function is declared with `WS_DLL_PUBLIC`, it should be treated as part of the API and left there, as it's there for dissectors to use even if no bundled dissectors use it.

Otherwise, it's a target for removal, as it's not intended to be used outside Wireshark's source code, and perhaps it no longer serves a purpose.

Typical examples (there are currently 2152) would be:

Note: epan/dissectors/packet-xml.c (0000000000002220 T xml_get_attrib) is not referred to so could be static? (declared in header but not referred to)

Note: epan/dissectors/packet-xml.c (0000000000002500 T xml_get_cdata) is not referred to so could be static? (declared in header but not referred to)

Note: epan/dissectors/packet-xml.c (00000000000021b0 T xml_get_tag) is not referred to so could be static? (declared in header but not referred to)

These functions are only called inside packet-xml.c, but are included in packet-xml.h.  They are not declared with WS_DLL_PUBLIC.  I am guilty sometimes of having functions that are not marked with WS_DLL_PUBLIC, but were only called from private dissectors (built-in dissectors on a private branch).  An example would be set_pdcp_lte_up_ciphering_key() in packet-pdcp-lte.h.  I would be happy to add WS_DLL_PUBLIC in that situation.

The way I've used check_static.py has mostly been:

./tools/check_static.py | grep -v "in header"

to find definitions that should be static or are not used at all and ought to be deleted.  I think we could probably remove lots of definitions from header files, and at the same time:

* make quite a few definitions static (if this change hasn't already outed them)
* re-order some definitions and/or add forward declarations instead
* delete quite a few functions that were added but never (or not for a while) used

The downside would be that some small number of people might lose something that their private builds previously relied upon.

> The downside would be that some small number of people might lose something that their private builds previously relied upon.

It's possible that this happened for some of the variables marked static now, if they were used by in-tree third party dissectors and not marked in a header. Hopefully people will complain. Hopefully (this has proven to be too much of an ask in the past), people with such dissectors will at least try to compile them against the upcoming 4.7.0 release.

This only tracks variables; the other warning for functions that are not static but also not declared in a header is harder to enable because of the registration functions. So I don't think we can drop `check_static.py` entirely, I guess?

> the other warning for functions that are not static but also not declared in a header is harder to enable because of the registration functions.

Would it make sense to have tools/make-regs.py generate a file that declares all the registration functions and have all dissectors include that file? It might fix that, although it might slow down compilation a bit.

> Would it make sense to have tools/make-regs.py generate a file that declares all the registration functions and have all dissectors include that file?

Perhaps have `tools/make-regs.py` generate a file that declares all the registration functions, and have `config.h` include that file, and then all the dissectors get that as a transitive include?

I guess that is used outside of libwireshark so it's a bad idea. But having be included by an existing file in epan might work, or we could make a new file that is mandatory for all in tree dissectors.
This breaks compilation on NetBSD 10, whose Heimdal krb5.h file declares `krb5_context` as a typedef for `struct krb5_context_data`, *not* as a typedef for `struct _krb5_context`.

> This breaks compilation on NetBSD 10, whose Heimdal krb5.h file declares `krb5_context` as a typedef for `struct krb5_context_data`, _not_ as a typedef for `struct _krb5_context`.

+add_custom_target(plugins)

+	codecs/l24
+	${CUSTOM_PLUGIN_SRC_DIR}
+)
+set(STRATOSHARK_PLUGIN_SRC_DIRS)
+if(SINSP_FOUND)
+	list(APPEND STRATOSHARK_PLUGIN_SRC_DIRS

+endif()
+if(SPANDSP_FOUND)
+	list(APPEND WIRESHARK_PLUGIN_SRC_DIRS

+	)
+endif()
+if(BCG729_FOUND)
+	list(APPEND WIRESHARK_PLUGIN_SRC_DIRS
+		codecs/G729
+	)
+endif()
+if(AMRNB_FOUND)
+	list(APPEND WIRESHARK_PLUGIN_SRC_DIRS
+		codecs/amrnb
+	)
+endif()
+if(AMRWB_FOUND)
+	list(APPEND WIRESHARK_PLUGIN_SRC_DIRS
+		codecs/amrwb
+	)
+endif()
+if(ILBC_FOUND)
+	list(APPEND WIRESHARK_PLUGIN_SRC_DIRS
+		codecs/iLBC
+	)
+endif()
+if(OPUS_FOUND)
+	list(APPEND WIRESHARK_PLUGIN_SRC_DIRS
+		codecs/opus_dec
+	)
+endif()
+if(SBC_FOUND)
+	list(APPEND WIRESHARK_PLUGIN_SRC_DIRS
+		codecs/sbc
+	)
+endif()
+
+# Build demo plugin, only if asked explicitly
+if(ENABLE_PLUGIN_IFDEMO)
+	list(APPEND WIRESHARK_PLUGIN_SRC_DIRS
+		ui/pluginifdemo
+	)
+endif()
+
+# Plugins are required to define some versioning variables, which blocks this.
+# XXX - Introduce a plugin header that declares them?
+# Clang has -Wmissing-variable-declarations for C and C++, gcc only for C
+if(C_Wmissing_variable_declarations_VALID)
+	add_compile_options("$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C>:-Wno-error=missing-variable-declarations>")
+endif()
+if(CXX_Wmissing_variable_declarations_VALID)
+	add_compile_options("$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:-Wno-error=missing-variable-declarations>")
+endif()
+
+foreach(_plugin_src_dir ${WIRESHARK_PLUGIN_SRC_DIRS} ${STRATOSHARK_PLUGIN_SRC_DIRS})
+	cmake_path(SET _plugins_dir "plugins")
+	cmake_path(IS_PREFIX _plugins_dir "${_plugin_src_dir}" _is_plugins_subdir)
+	# If custom in-tree plugins have the "plugins" prefix, strip it off
+	if(_is_plugins_subdir)
+		message(DEBUG "${_plugin_src_dir} is a subdir of plugins, removing prefix")
+		cmake_path(RELATIVE_PATH _plugin_src_dir BASE_DIRECTORY "${_plugins_dir}")
+	endif()
+	add_subdirectory( ${_plugin_src_dir} )
+endforeach()
